requirements.summary: A conversion is one sample cycle, one trial per bit from the most significant bit, then a one-cycle done with the code.
A start is taken only while ready; a start during a conversion is ignored; reset abandons a conversion; the array tracks the input until the end of the sample cycle and ignores it afterwards.
The real-number model of the capacitor DAC decides every trial as exact arithmetic does, on both sides of every threshold and for every code.

At a settled clock the real-number model and ngspice give the same codes and the same top-plate voltage within the stated tolerance, also beyond the rails, and the logic replays the ngspice decisions consistently.
The nominal array has no missing code; the mismatched array loses the predicted codes; the transfer stays monotonic.

The ngspice waveforms follow the closed forms; codes at short clock periods follow the sampling shortfall formula; the model is valid above the computed minimum period and visibly wrong in ngspice only below it.
Solver tolerances, step limits and the integration method do not change a code or move the top plate beyond the tolerance.
